title: REDAgentBench: Executable Red Teaming and Faithful Measurement of LLM Agent Systems
authors: Chen, Liu, Zhu, Dou, Jiang, Li, Guo, Chen & Zhang
research_question: Can red-teaming and faithful measurement of tool-using agents be made executable and evidence-grounded?
evaluator_type: three view-specific evaluators over ONE fixed judge backbone (Qwen3.7-plus): Trajectory Judge, State Judge, Hybrid Judge; plus deterministic rule-first verifiers
ground_truth: YES - stratified sample of 360 valid GPT-5.2 rollouts labelled by two blinded reviewers with a third adjudicating; separately 480 case versions reviewed by two security experts and 320 frozen cases audited blinded
judge_reliability: Human inter-reviewer agreement 91.94% (kappa = 0.838) before adjudication; judge audit precision 97.84% (95% CI 96.00-99.28), recall 91.27% (88.58-93.80), accuracy 93.62% (91.57-95.44); raw judged ASR 55.43% versus human-audited 59.42%
judge_validity: CENTRAL - fixed-rollout judging-configuration audit: State Judge reports ASR 7.73-11.72 pp higher than Trajectory Judge for every model; 12.97-21.20% of paired labels change; all six paired differences significant under exact McNemar p <= 6.54e-5; 43 strict pairwise reversals across 23 of 64 slices. Mechanism: 'a trajectory-view may suggest safety, while the state-view confirms harm'; agents sometimes refuse only AFTER the harmful write
judge_attack: Not the focus - no judge prompt-injection or adversarial-judge stress test; judge calibration at a single operating point, no ROC
defense_evaluation: YES - section 4.6 replays a training-free policy reminder and measures it with the STATE oracle: ASR reduced by 74.19 pp (95% source-case cluster CI 69.85-78.41) on 510 matched pairs, 368 of 434 baseline harmful executions prevented; neutral control ~ baseline
agent_security: YES - 1,661 executable cases, 5 service surfaces, 6 models, 3 harnesses (Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw)
exact_overlap: Formalises reported ASR as exposure-execution-observation-adjudication; formalises view-specific judging configuration c=(v,p,g) over backbone b; holds rollouts fixed while varying the judging configuration; measures evaluator-induced ranking inversions; validates against blinded humans; re-measures a defense with an oracle
relevance: *** DECISIVE FOR THE PASS-7 NO-GO. *** The candidate's core experiment - same underlying trajectory, different evaluator framing, different labels - has been run on agents, with a cleaner design (rollout literally held fixed), human ground truth, a published significance test and demonstrated ranking inversions. The only surviving residual is a defense factor in the view audit, which is a factorial extension of this design
status: A - full HTML v1 read in pass 7. NOTE: also catalogued as R53 (pass-3 abstract-only entry); R53 is superseded by this row

title: Know Thy Judge: On the Robustness Meta-Evaluation of LLM Safety Judges
venue: ICBINB Workshop at ICLR 2025; arXiv preprint
research_question: Can we trust the evaluations of the evaluators? Robustness meta-evaluation of LLM safety judges under in-the-wild factors and adversarial attacks
evaluator_type: LLM-as-a-judge safety moderators (specific judge set not captured at abstract level)
ground_truth: YES - human-labelled safety datasets; comparisons are 'on the same dataset'
judge_validity: *** 'small changes such as the style of the model output can lead to jumps of up to 0.24 in the false negative rate on the same dataset' *** - surface nuisance varied at fixed ground truth
judge_attack: *** YES - 'adversarial attacks on the model generation can fool some judges into misclassifying 100% of harmful generations as safe ones' ***
agent_security: NO - safety judges on harmful generations, not agent trajectories
exact_overlap: Style/surface manipulation at fixed ground truth and adversarial manipulation of a judge via the judged generation; the conclusion 'low attack success under certain judges could create a false sense of security' is the candidate's motivation stated verbatim
relevance: Directly pre-empts the candidate's Part F 'style condition' experiment and establishes the phenomenon with an effect size. Cited by R77 as prior work showing style, manipulation, bias and instance-level errors distort judge labels

title: Security in LLM-as-a-Judge: A Comprehensive SoK
authors: Al Masoud, Anju, Arazzi, Cihangiroglu, Kembu, Nicolazzo, Nocera, Vinod P & Sakthidharan
venue: arXiv preprint (University of Pavia; Cochin University of Science and Technology)
research_question: What is known about the security of LLM-as-a-Judge systems, and what remains open?
evaluator_type: systematisation across five roles: judge as attack TARGET, judge as attack INSTRUMENT, judge as DEFENCE tool, judge as object of evaluation, judge as evaluation strategy in security domains
ground_truth: not applicable (systematisation); quality filter required Q1 journals or A*/A conferences, with preprints admitted only where an author has >5000 citations
judge_validity: Provides the taxonomy and the open-problem list; section 8.3 is titled 'Length and Style Bias Exploitation'
judge_attack: Catalogs judge attacks with effect sizes: JudgeDeceiver (CCS 2024), BadJudge (1% poisoning -> 3x score inflation; backdoored guardrails misclassify toxic as safe 83.9%), Emoji Attack (ShieldLM 71.9% -> 3.5%, i.e. no arXiv id captured), master-key (FPR up to 80% across 10 keys and 5 benchmarks), RIPD (accuracy down 9.5% helpfulness / 27.9% harmlessness at ~0.85 benchmark agreement), Maloyan & Namiot prompt injection (max ASR 73.8%), Li et al. robustness (PAIR+Combined ~70% ASR on GPT-4o; up to 40% variation across prompt templates)

relevance: The existence of a dedicated SoK means the field already treats the evaluator as an attack surface and has named style bias exploitation as a challenge. The SoK frames the OPEN problem as designing detection/defence mechanisms, not as measuring defense-dependent judge error in agent security

title: BadJudge: backdoor vulnerabilities of LLM-as-a-judge
research_question: Can an adversary manipulate evaluation outcomes by poisoning a judge during training or at web scale?
evaluator_type: LLM-as-a-judge as candidate scorer (point-wise and pair-wise)
ground_truth: none reported; score inflation is measured against clean behaviour

relevance: The defence-independent version of the candidate's concern: the evaluator can be systematically wrong in a direction that favours or disfavours a system

title: Rubrics as an attack surface: stealthy preference drift in LLM judges (RIPD)
authors: Ding, Pang, Sun, Wang, Wu & Deng
research_question: Can an adversary steer a judge's preferences purely through natural-language rubric edits, with no access to parameters, data or inputs?
evaluator_type: LLM judge generating preference labels for downstream alignment; rubrics as the manipulation channel
ground_truth: YES - a trusted human reference on target domains, plus benchmark validation sets
judge_reliability: benchmark agreement stays ~0.85 while target-domain labels flip - i.e. reliability on the benchmark masks invalidity on the target domain
judge_validity: *** Biased Rubric Search reduces judge accuracy by up to 9.5% on helpfulness and 27.9% on harmlessness; bias transfers across judge models (Qwen3-14B, Gemma-3-27B-it, DeepSeek-V3); propagated into downstream DPO post-training ***; and 'the biased rubrics consistently received higher quality ratings from independent evaluators than the original seed rubrics'
judge_attack: YES - the evaluation protocol itself is the attack surface
exact_overlap: An evaluator-CONFIGURATION change that alters measured safety while appearing legitimate and while benchmark validation still passes. Structurally the same argument the candidate would make about defenses
relevance: The closest published instance of 'the measurement instrument changed, the conclusion changed, and it looked fine on the validation set'. Strongly pre-empts a defense-as-rubric-perturbation framing

title: Comparison requires valid measurement: Rethinking attack success rate comparisons in AI red teaming
authors: Chouldechova, Cooper, Barocas, Palia, Vann & Wallach
research_question: When can attack success rates be meaningfully compared?
evaluator_type: formal measurement-theory framing: ASR as a measurement of an estimand defined by a probabilistic threat model M = (s, D, C); judge J as the operationalisation of the oracle success criteria s
ground_truth: conceptual, via the oracle/judge distinction; empirical work uses human preference-style labels on jailbreaking
judge_reliability: reliability explicitly set aside: 'not simply reliability issues (sampling variation)'
judge_validity: CENTRAL - section 5 is entirely about judge/measurement validity: E(ASR) = TPR(J;s)*alpha + FPR(J;s)*(1-alpha); differential TPR/FPR across systems and across jailbreak approaches biases ASR; EQUAL OVERALL ACCURACY OR AUC IS INSUFFICIENT
judge_attack: Not framed as attacking the judge; framed as systematic mismeasurement by the judge
defense_evaluation: NO - no defense comparison, no agent setting
agent_security: NO - jailbreaking is the running example ('broadly applicable to ASRs obtained via other AI red teaming approaches')
exact_overlap: The theoretical account of defense-dependent (system-dependent) evaluator error, in closed form, with the inversion condition
relevance: Supplies the theoretical half of the candidate's decomposition and declares validity to be the paper's own focus. The candidate would be working inside their stated scope
status: A - full HTML v1 read in pass 6

title: Attack Success Rate Is Not a Number: On Measurement Validity in Agentic AI Security Evaluation
research_question: ASR is not a single quantity but a family parameterised by six design choices papers seldom specify
evaluator_type: six-axis decomposition of ASR; A2 (success oracle) covers string/regex, LLM judge, environment state and human adjudication
ground_truth: hand-coded random sample of 50 papers (seed 1234) for reporting practice; no judge ground truth produced
judge_reliability: variance/CI reported by 23.9% of papers; calibration reported by 29.7% of judge-using papers; LLM judge used by at least 24.7%
judge_validity: *** 'Defenses change the distribution of trajectories - more refusals, more hedging, more truncation - so an uncalibrated judge's error rate is not constant across the systems being compared. That is precisely the condition under which ranking fails to be preserved.' *** Also: four oracle families 'disagree in both directions'; a judge 'is a measurement taken through an instrument whose calibration is seldom reported'
defense_evaluation: No defense run end to end: 'We have not run defenses end to end, so we report no empirical ranking inversion'
exact_overlap: States the candidate's mechanism verbatim as a diagnosis, with the A2 oracle axis and checklist item 10 on utility
relevance: Names the exact mechanism (defense changes trajectory distribution -> judge error is not constant across compared systems) without measuring it. So the candidate's hypothesis is not new; only its agent-specific quantification would be - and R77 has largely supplied that
